name: Tally <> GoHighLevel & Google Sheets Sync - Ledgers, Outstanding Balances & Customer Records

parameters.content:
# Tally <> GoHighLevel + Google Sheets Sync (ledgers, outstanding & customer records)

Sales lives in GoHighLevel, the money lives in Tally, and the two drift apart within a week: reps chase customers who already paid, credit-hold customers get new orders, and new customers never make it into Tally. This workflow keeps them in step, with Tally as the financial source of truth and a human approval step before anything is written into the books.

## How it works
1. **Apply approved changes first.** Rows your accountant marked **Approved** in the Tally Change Queue are turned into Tally import XML (new ledgers, contact updates, receipt vouchers), posted to Tally, and the response is written back.
2. **Export from Tally** over its XML/HTTP interface: all debtor ledgers (with GUID and ALTERID) and the Bills Receivable report.
3. **Read GoHighLevel**: contacts and recent successful payments, via the API v2 with pagination.
4. **Sync engine** links ledgers to contacts (saved link, then email, phone, company name), computes balance, overdue, aging buckets and credit status per customer, and does a **three-way merge** of email and phone using the last agreed value, so edits on either side flow the right way and edits on both sides become conflicts instead of overwrites.
5. **Tally -> GHL (automatic):** custom fields, AR tags (current, overdue 30/60/90, credit hold, advance) and new contacts for ledgers not in GHL. Only changed values are sent.
6. **GHL -> Tally (approval):** new customer ledgers, contact edits and receipt vouchers for GHL payments (matched to the open bill when possible) go to the queue.
7. **Sheets mirror + Slack:** Customers, Bills (with cleared bills), Conflicts and the queue. Slack is only pinged when a person needs to act.

## Setup steps
1. Tally Prime: F1 Help > Settings > Connectivity, enable **Client/Server = Both** on port 9000, keep the company open. n8n must reach that machine (same network, VPN or a tunnel).
2. Create a Sheet with tabs **Customers, Bills, Tally Change Queue, Conflicts** (headers in the notes) and paste the ID into every Sheets node.
3. Connect a **HighLevel OAuth2** credential (contacts and payments scopes) in the GHL nodes, plus Google Sheets and Slack.
4. In GHL create the custom fields listed in **Set Sync Rules** and paste their IDs, plus your location ID, Tally URL, company and receipt bank ledger.
5. Test against a **copy of your Tally company** first. Keep autoApproveTallyWrites off.

## 1. Schedule & rules
Every 2 hours, 9 AM-7 PM, Mon-Sat. **Set Sync Rules** holds Tally URL/company/debtor group, GHL location and custom field IDs, AR tag names, credit-hold days, receipt bank ledger and switches for creating contacts and syncing contact fields back to Tally.

## 2. Load sync state
**Customers:** Tally GUID, Tally Ledger, Tally Alter ID, GHL Contact ID, Match Method, Email, Phone, GSTIN, State, Closing Balance, Overdue Amount, Overdue 1-30, Overdue 31-60, Overdue 61-90, Overdue 90+, Oldest Due Date, Max Overdue Days, Open Bills, Credit Limit, Credit Status, Snapshot Email, Snapshot Phone, Last Synced
**Bills:** Bill Key, Party, Bill Ref, Bill Date, Due Date, Outstanding, Overdue Days, Status, Cleared On, Last Seen
To link a ledger manually, paste the GHL Contact ID into its Customers row.

## 3. Post approved changes to Tally (runs first)
**Tally Change Queue:** Change Key, Created On, Type, Tally Ledger, GHL Contact ID, Summary, Payload, Status, Applied On, Tally Response
Set Status to **Approved** to post a row, **Rejected** to drop it. Each row is sent as its own import so one error cannot block the rest. Tally's CREATED / ALTERED / ERRORS counts decide Applied or Failed.

## 4. Export from Tally, read GHL
Two XML export requests (debtor ledgers via a TDL collection, then Bills Receivable), parsed in code with Tally's sign convention (debit = negative). GHL contacts come from the search API, payments from the transactions API, both paged.

## 5. Sync engine
One Code node emits a typed record for every action. Duplicate matches, name-only matches, both-sides edits and payments from unlinked contacts become Conflicts rather than guesses. The router sends each record type to its branch.

## 6. Sheets mirror
**Conflicts:** Conflict Key, Detected On, Type, Tally Ledger, GHL Contact ID, Tally Value, GHL Value, Detail, Status. Mark Resolved once fixed.
Bills no longer returned by Tally are marked Cleared with the date.

## 7. Push to GoHighLevel
Only changed custom fields and contact details are sent. AR tags are added and removed separately so other tags are untouched. New contacts are upserted by email/phone and their IDs saved back to Customers. Batched to stay inside GHL rate limits.

## 8. Notify only when needed
Slack gets a message only if something was posted to Tally, a write failed, new changes await approval, a conflict appeared, a payment could not be linked, or a customer newly went on credit hold.

## Credentials & security
Tally's HTTP interface has no authentication, so never expose port 9000 to the internet; use a VPN or a tunnel with access control. GHL uses OAuth2 and Google/Slack OAuth2. Tally is only written through the approval queue, with a fixed set of fields (email, mobile, new ledgers, receipts).
